key_insight: Mutually incompatible martensitic variants in Ti₇₆Nb₂₂Al₂ can support a fine-scale microstructure with no macroscopic deformation through a degenerate T₁₂ configuration.
engineering_relevance: The analysis helps explain how shape-memory alloys can transform without deforming grain boundaries and why certain variant interfaces occur more frequently.
method: Apply the moving-mask approximation to 12 martensitic gradients rank-one connected to austenite.
Establish a degenerate T₁₂ configuration under unit middle eigenvalue and volume preservation, with microstructures supported on just 8 gradients.
Analyze pairwise near-compatibility to interpret observed interface frequencies.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports experimental confirmation of an identity macroscopic deformation gradient and associates more nearly compatible variant pairs with more frequently observed interfaces.
watch_item: The exact construction assumes unit middle eigenvalue and volume preservation; no deformation with the same boundary condition has its gradient in the finite variant set almost everywhere.
paper_title: Complex Martensitic Microstructures in ${\rm Ti}_{76}{\rm Nb}_{22}{\rm Al}_{2}$
